notes: Read all six units, full federal-budget context, all ten candidates and the review. Restored the United States federal budget process to every standalone assertion and identified the annual spending, debt and reviewed one-third as federal. Preserved the inflation qualification. Restored the source's explicit evaluations that the accounting is deceptive and irresponsible and that federal budget review is a sham.

claims.claim_text: The U.S. federal budget process assumes every spending project remains permanently even when law provides for expiration.
The U.S. federal budget process assumes tax relief is temporary.
The U.S. federal budget process treats tax cuts as spending, equating Americans retaining earnings with additional pork-project spending.
The U.S. federal budget process fails to recognize lower tax rates' positive effect on economic growth.
The platform calls federal budget accounting deceptive and irresponsible because it records a below-inflation program-funding increase as a decrease.
After a budget is produced under the U.S. federal process, federal budget law limits congressional consideration time before a vote.
The platform characterizes the U.S. federal budget review process as a sham because only one-third of $3 trillion in annual federal spending receives yearly budget and appropriations review.
The remaining $2 trillion in annual U.S. federal spending automatically funds national-debt interest or entitlements.
The U.S. federal budget process assumes automatic spending increases.
Debate over the annually reviewed one-third of U.S. federal spending addresses only how much additional spending to approve.
